text: Feedback. The coach gave me feedback after every heat.
Praise. He does not give praise very often.
Advice. She gave me one piece of advice and it worked.
Warning. The lifeguard gave us a warning about the rocks.
Promise. He made a promise and he kept it.
Complain. Nobody complains about the waves here.
Admit. He admitted that he had made a mistake.
Mention. She mentioned that the tide was dropping.
He said that I was too slow.
She told me my second wave was better.
He said, and I quote,
What did he say?
She told me to wait for the sets.
My host family said that dinner is at seven.
Sorry, what did she say exactly?

Right, sit down. Three things. Your first wave was a mistake and you know it was, because you told me before the heat that you were going to wait for the sets. You did not wait. Second, your take-off is too slow, and it has been too slow all season, so that is what we work on from Monday. Third, and I am only saying this once: the conditions were difficult for everybody out there and you were the only one who read the tide correctly. Do not tell anybody I said that.

So what did he say? Tell me everything. Right, so he said your first wave was a mistake, which honestly everybody could see. And he told you that your take-off has been too slow all season, which is fair. But then he said you were the only one who read the tide correctly, and he asked you not to repeat it? That is the biggest compliment that man has given anybody this year. My brother trained with him for three seasons and he told me he never once said anything nice. Not once.
